questions.q: What does 'Der Zug hat Verspätung' mean?
questions.explain: 'Verspätung haben' means 'to be delayed/late', so 'Der Zug hat Verspätung' = 'The train is delayed'.
'Verreisen' means 'to go away/travel (somewhere)'.

questions.q: How do you say 'The hotel was right by the beach'?
options: Das Hotel war direkt an der Straße
Das Hotel war direkt am Strand
Das Hotel ist direkt am Strand
Das Hotel war weit vom Strand
questions.explain: 'War' = 'was', 'direkt am Strand' = 'right by the beach'; 'Straße' (street) is the trap.
'Das Oktoberfest' is the famous folk festival/funfair held in Munich.
'Sich verlaufen' means 'to get lost' while walking; 'sich verfahren' = to get lost while driving.

questions.q: What does 'das Viertel' mean (in a town)?
questions.explain: 'Das Viertel' means 'the neighbourhood/district' of a town (also 'a quarter' in time).
'Das Ausland' means 'abroad/foreign countries'; 'im Ausland' = abroad.

questions.q: How do you say 'My bedroom is upstairs'?
questions.explain: 'Das Schlafzimmer' = 'bedroom' and 'oben' = 'upstairs'; 'unten' (downstairs) is the trap.
'Die Reise' means 'the journey/trip'; 'der Reis' (rice) is the near-miss.
'In der Nähe' means 'nearby/close by', e.g. 'in der Nähe der Schule' = 'near the school'.

questions.q: What does 'gemütlich' mean (e.g. of a room)?
questions.explain: 'Gemuetlich' means 'cosy/comfortable', a typical word for a homely room.
'Die Fußgängerzone' is the 'pedestrian zone/precinct' (from 'Fußgänger' = pedestrian).

questions.q: How do you say 'We spent the holidays by the sea'?
options: Wir haben die Ferien am Meer gebraucht
Wir haben die Ferien in den Bergen verbracht
Wir haben die Ferien am Meer verbracht
Wir verbringen die Ferien am Meer
questions.explain: 'Am Meer' = 'by the sea' and 'verbracht' (perfect of 'verbringen') = 'spent'; 'gebraucht' (needed) is the trap.
'Der Bahnhof' means 'the train station'; a bus stop is 'die Haltestelle'.

questions.q: How do you say 'We are flying to Spain'?
questions.explain: 'Fliegen nach' = 'to fly to' and 'Spanien' = Spain.
'Packen' = 'to pack' and 'die Koffer' = 'the suitcases', so this means 'to pack the suitcases'.
'Die Grenze' means 'the border/frontier' between countries.
'Das Rathaus' means 'the town hall' (from 'Rat' = council), not anything to do with rats.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'The shops are closed on Sundays'?
questions.explain: 'Geschlossen' = 'closed', 'sonntags' = 'on Sundays'; 'geöffnet' (open) is the trap.
'Die Ferienwohnung' means 'a holiday flat/self-catering apartment'.
'Das Gepäck' means 'the luggage/baggage'.
'Im Ausland' means 'abroad'. 'Das Ausland' = foreign countries; 'das Inland' = home country.
